definitions.explanation: A gathering held to see off someone who is departing — a transferring colleague, a graduating student, a person going abroad. Slightly more formal and celebratory in tone than {送別会|そうべつかい}, emphasizing well-wishing rather than parting.

examples.japanese: {歓送会|かんそうかい}を{開|ひら}く。
{留学生|りゅうがくせい}の{歓送会|かんそうかい}に{招|まね}かれました。
examples.english: I was invited to the send-off party for the exchange students.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}の{歓送会|かんそうかい}では、{部長|ぶちょう}が{挨拶|あいさつ}をすることになっている。
examples.english: At next week's send-off party, the department head is scheduled to give a speech.

notes:
From {歓送|かんそう} (giving a warm send-off) + {会|かい} (gathering). Typical of workplaces and schools at the spring transfer season, and often paired with a welcome party as {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歓送会|かんそうかい}を{開|ひら}く: to hold a send-off party
- {歓送会|かんそうかい}に{出席|しゅっせき}する: to attend a send-off party
- {歓送会|かんそうかい}の{幹事|かんじ}: the organizer of a send-off party

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {送別会|そうべつかい}: farewell party — the everyday word; interchangeable in most contexts but focuses on the parting
- {歓迎会|かんげいかい}: welcome party — the counterpart, held for new arrivals

cross_references.headword: {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}
cross_references.label: combined welcome and farewell party
